payload.title: Source-against-translation checks
payload.description:
As an editor, I want automatic checks that read the English block and its translation together, so a translation that changes a number, drops a link or loses a hedge is caught by code before any person looks.

Design: section 2.5. New `check` request shape with an optional `source` (text, language, block alignment). Rules lane: `parity` detectors for numbers, dates and units compared as parsed values, names and do-not-translate terms, links, citation keys, images, Markus structure, quotations, code, block coverage and length ratio. Judgment lane: a bilingual judge marking spans with MQM categories, quoting both sides (code confirms the quotes exist); a block counts as clean only when repeated passes agree. Faithfulness findings at `error` hold publication; monolingual findings never do.

Ryan 2026-11-13: respect the target locale's conventions (naming, register, press norms) through the per-language glossary and pack, but never omit or alter a factual claim. Parity therefore accepts an approved localized form of a name and rejects a dropped or changed claim. This is automated evaluation only: no native-reader panel anywhere in this story. Back-translation is a reading aid, never a check input or a gate.

```gherkin
Feature: A translation says what the original says
  Scenario: The same date written two ways matches
    Given the source block says "in December 2025"
    And the translated block says "2025 年 12 月"
    When Humanus compares them
    Then no number finding is reported

  Scenario: A changed number is an error
    Given the source block says "68 percent"
    And the translated block says "86%"
    When Humanus compares them
    Then an error finding names both values

  Scenario Outline: What must survive translation unchanged
    Given a source block with <thing>
    And a translated block without it
    When Humanus compares them
    Then an error finding names the missing <thing>

    Examples:
      | thing                        |
      | a link                       |
      | a citation key               |
      | a do-not-translate name      |
      | a quotation                  |
      | a code span                  |

  Scenario: A glossary term must be used
    Given the glossary says "disclosure" is "披露" in Chinese
    And the translated block uses "泄露"
    When Humanus compares them
    Then a terminology finding offers "披露"

  Scenario: A locale's naming convention is respected without dropping the claim
    Given the glossary gives the approved Chinese form of an organisation's name
    And the translated block uses the approved form and keeps every claim of the source sentence
    When Humanus compares them
    Then no finding is reported

  Scenario: A dropped hedge is a faithfulness error
    Given the source block says "may have leaked"
    And the translated block says "leaked" with no hedge
    When the bilingual judge reads both blocks in repeated passes that agree
    Then an error finding quotes both sides and names the changed certainty
```
